explanation: Inclusive positive partial sums remove division by zero. The block bound >=1-S_m/S_n violates the Cauchy criterion at epsilon=1/2, while a_(n+1)/S_(n+1)^2 is bounded by 1/S_n-1/S_(n+1), a convergent telescoping series. Tail invariance supplies the omitted initial term. The higher-exponent refinement is orientation only, not a used theorem.

explanation: Eventual membership gives identical set liminf and limsup. Domination by finite-measure D gives finite union and limit-set measure, so the two measure inequalities force equal finite numerical liminf and limsup. From their tail-bound definitions, for epsilon>0 a sufficiently late tail has inf>mu(E)-epsilon and sup<mu(E)+epsilon, proving the last real convergence assertion directly; no missing substantial squeeze prerequisite.
